subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land the bounded provider-normalized tool-schema parameter cache now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-visible, but the permanent lifecycle and cache boundary affect provider hook ownership, custom provider behavior, plugin metadata preservation, and the prepared-runtime rollout.

options.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or land the open cache PR with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Fold into prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider/tool facts to remove repeated hot-path work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini or heap-profile before/after evidence confirms the user-visible impact on a real provider path.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or land the open cache PR with the same bounded shape: cache cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: mcaxtr owns the adjacent prepared-runtime tracker, which is the clearest maintainer signal for deciding whether this cache lands independently or waits for the broader migration.
